source: LidarBC 2025 1 m DSM minus DTM (flown 2025-07-06..26), tiles listed in apex-media/_mountain/dem/lidarbc_raw/urls.txt

rasters.note: Row 0 = north. Cell (r,c) covers game x in [originX+5c, originX+5c+5), z in [originZ+5r, ...). Same 5 m step as terrain.json but a larger extent (game x -382..3718, z -462..3138 vs terrain grid 0..3220, 0..2640) so it also covers a ~380-500 m ring outside the playable terrain grid.

encoding.cover: uint8 = fraction of 1 m cells with canopy >2.5 m * 255
encoding.height: uint8 = max canopy height in the cell (m) * 4, same scale as horizon-canopy.u8

horizonPatch.note: Drop-in replacement for horizon-canopy.u8 cells (horizon.json grid, 60 m) that fall inside the LiDAR extent: horizon[(row0+i)*454+(col0+j)] = patch[i*cols+j]. canopy = mean(DSM-DTM)*4 like the MRDEM layer; cover = tree fraction*255 (extra).

stands.note: LiDAR forest polygons (20 m smoothed cover classes 0.2-0.5 open, >=0.5 closed) only OUTSIDE the terrain grid, to seed distant-forest placement. WGS84.

calibration.note: Over the 59x68 horizon cells covered by LiDAR (4,012 cells), apron.ts coverAt() = clamp((MRDEM canopy-1.5)/7) gives mean cover 0.76 vs LiDAR-measured 0.49 (corr 0.68). It overestimates cover in forest (MRDEM >=6 m -> 0.84-1.0 vs LiDAR 0.44-0.68) and underestimates open/sparse ground (MRDEM <3 m -> 0.03 vs LiDAR 0.14).
calibration.suggestedFit: cover ~= clamp(0.15 + 0.039*h, 0, 0.72) where h = MRDEM canopy metres (least squares on the overlap). Applies near Apex only; extrapolate with care.
calibration.implication: If distant forest looks sparse in game, the MRDEM-based cover is not the cause in this overlap (it is already higher than measured). Tree instance density/LOD in the apron is the more likely lever. [inferred]
